meta.strictDefinition: Strict single-entry means one paid entry total for the entire tournament. One entry per flight, a 1Day label, or silence in a structure sheet does not meet that definition.

hotelNotes.title: No independent quality ranking or timed walking score

known: Research snapshot is Nov 16, 2026. Tournament dates, terms, hotel fees, availability, and room rates can change; check the official source again before paying.
No upcoming event in the reviewed official sources is confirmed as strict single-entry (one paid entry total). The confirmed strict-entry list is empty by design.
WPT Prime runs Dec 5–12 with a $1,100 entry and $5M guarantee; its structure allows one entry plus one re-entry per starting flight, so it is not single-entry.
PGT ARIA High Roller events run Nov 28–Dec 2 and explicitly allow unlimited re-entry. Official schedule/news and structure conflict on start time and cost; unresolved fields stay blank.

Reviewed Venetian $600 events labeled 1Day do not state a strict one-entry cap. Its multi-flight structures say a player who bags for Day 2 cannot play a later flight; that restriction does not establish one entry total.
Daily Caesars Palace, Horseshoe, and MGM Grand starts are published, but their event entry caps are not confirmed in the reviewed sources.
The listed nightly resort fees are fee components, not room quotes. The four-night fee-only subtotals are transparent multiplication of the posted nightly amount and are not a full stay total.
Treasure Island's official property map confirms pedestrian bridges to Venetian/Palazzo but does not publish walking minutes.
missing: A strict one-entry total confirmed in an official structure for any upcoming tournament.
A comparable, date-specific Dec 3–7, 2026 room quote including room price, resort fee, taxes, and mandatory charges. Official booking searches did not return usable totals.
Exact route minutes from each hotel entrance/room to the poker tournament room, including internal resort walk time and accessible routing.
Venetian event-specific total-entry/re-entry limits for the sampled 1Day and multi-flight events.
Day-specific entry limits, registration cutoff, current buy-in, and guaranteed pool for all daily Caesars/Horseshoe/MGM tournaments.
A confirmed current year/date for MGM's linked $120 schedule and Bellagio's recurring Friday/Sunday structure sheets.
A resolution from PGT/Wynn on the ARIA series' conflicting start time and cost presentation; no independent hotel-quality score or guaranteed room availability.
questions: Venetian Tournament Desk: for each shortlisted event, is there exactly one paid entry for the whole event, or can a player re-enter / enter another flight? What is the latest registration time?
Wynn / PGT: for ARIA High Roller events, which start time is current (12 PM or 3 PM), and is the $5,300 schedule figure inclusive of the structure's $5,000 buy-in plus fees?
Caesars Palace and Horseshoe: what are today's buy-in, guarantee, re-entry/add-on rules, and registration cutoff for the specific daily start?
MGM Grand and Bellagio: are the linked tournament sheets current for the intended date, and what are the precise entry, gratuity/add-on, and late-registration terms?
Hotel booking desks: can you quote Dec 3–7, 2026 for two adults/one standard room, itemizing room rate, resort fee, taxes, and other mandatory charges?
For any hotel shortlist: can the property provide an entrance-to-poker-room accessible walking route and realistic minutes? Current official pages do not give a timed route.

suggestions.title: Keep the entry-rule gate strict
suggestions.text: Preserve separate states for confirmed single-entry, re-entry allowed, and entry cap unknown. Require an official structure sentence before promoting any candidate into the strict list.

suggestions.title: Add a trip-date quote workspace
suggestions.text: Let a traveler set check-in/out, guest count, room count, and a fee/tax-inclusive budget. Store a date-stamped hotel quote and its cancellation terms rather than estimating a full stay from resort fees.

suggestions.title: Add a route-time map only after verification
suggestions.text: Capture room entrance and poker-room pins, step-free routes, and source/date for each duration. Until then, show on-property or bridge-connected status without minutes.

suggestions.title: Model the maximum entry spend
suggestions.text: For each selected tournament, show base entry, permitted re-entries, optional add-ons/gratuities, and a user-set hard cap separately. Never label extra chips as a better-value buy-in by default.

suggestions.title: Make overlapping starts explicit alternatives
suggestions.text: Add a side-by-side comparison for events starting within the same window. Keep late-start events as conditional pivots only after elimination/finish and only while registration remains open.

suggestions.title: Add freshness checks before automation
suggestions.text: If schedule scraping is added later, retain the official PDF/page link, retrieval timestamp, and conflict state for every field; require a human review before declaring a strict-entry event.

decisionPaths.title: If one-entry total is non-negotiable
decisionPaths.text: Do not choose a tournament from this snapshot yet. Ask the room for the exact event's official terms; the strict-entry list remains empty until one paid entry total is documented.

decisionPaths.title: If one re-entry per flight is acceptable
decisionPaths.text: WPT Prime is the clearest published high-guarantee option in this sample: $1,100 / $5M, with one entry plus one re-entry per flight. Set a hard spend cap before registering.

decisionPaths.title: If a smaller posted entry matters most
decisionPaths.text: Venetian RaceDay Stack starts at $200 and the reviewed sheet shows no guarantee or total entry cap. Treat it as an unknown-policy candidate, not a freezeout, and ask the tournament desk first.

dayPlan.title: Start with a rules-and-budget check
dayPlan.text: No live 8 AM tournament was verified. Confirm today's official start, event number, exact buy-in, entry cap, late-registration cutoff, and your maximum total spend; do not assume yesterday's poster is current.

dayPlan.title: Pick one of the overlapping late-morning starts
dayPlan.text: For Dec 5, WPT Prime starts at 11 AM ($1,100 / $5M; one re-entry per flight). Venetian event #26 has an 11:10 AM $800 flight toward a $500K guarantee, but its total entry cap is not stated. These are alternatives at different venues—do not register for both.

dayPlan.title: Use the chosen venue's own registration desk
dayPlan.text: Wynn's general terms say event registration opens four hours before the scheduled start and registration is in the Wynn Poker Room. For another venue, confirm its current desk location and cutoff directly; no cross-resort walk time is assumed.

dayPlan.title: One start only; do not double-book
dayPlan.text: Choose WPT Prime Day 1A at Wynn (11:00 AM) OR Venetian #26 Day 1E (11:10 AM). Venetian's sheet prohibits a player who has bagged for Day 2 from playing a later flight, but does not establish the overall entry cap. The two rooms are not treated as a timed walk.

dayPlan.title: Only then consider a later session
dayPlan.text: Wynn's $600 NLH Turbo is posted for 9 PM with unlimited re-entry until level 9. It is a possible later choice only if the earlier event is over, the late-session budget allows it, and registration is still open. Do not assume a long event ends in time.
